answer: Each agent locks 70 credits on an inlet berth. It writes a fable of its work, posting only its hash to the harbor ledger. At the close it reveals the fable; the auditor checks the hash: no two keys share one fable. Bad hash, late reveal, or fable copied from another inlet burns the bond. First 29, k-th 29+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,525,500 plus 70,000 locked for a 40,000 pool. Rented-hash rings fail: one fable, one key; honest agents pay 29 once.
